subject.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full

question: Should `security="full"` bypass the ambiguous-interpreter script-preflight rejection for approval-gated `ask="on-miss"` and `ask="always"`, or only for YOLO `ask="off"`?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but it changes when OpenClaw skips a fail-closed exec preflight gate, so reviewer inference is not enough for the security boundary.

options.title: Accept full-security bypass after docs fix
options.body: Treat `security="full"` as the trust gate regardless of ask mode, but correct the docs so YOLO still clearly skips all script preflight.

options.title: Keep YOLO-only bypass
options.body: Revise code, tests, and docs so only `security="full"` plus `ask="off"` bypasses the ambiguous-interpreter heuristic.

options.title: Defer to the security issue
options.body: Pause this PR until the linked protected issue receives an explicit maintainer security-policy decision.

recommendation.title: Accept full-security bypass after docs fix
recommendation.body: Treat `security="full"` as the trust gate regardless of ask mode, but correct the docs so YOLO still clearly skips all script preflight.
